summary: Construct text from Unicode code point integers.
documentation: char returns a string whose characters correspond to its integer arguments, in argument order. It provides a direct way to construct known symbols from numeric data without confusing a Unicode value with a UTF-8 byte sequence.
inputs: symbols(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_code INTEGER NOT NULL, second_code INTEGER NOT NULL). Codes are valid Unicode scalar values excluding zero.
returns: id and the two-character string AS text, ordered by id.
caution: Validate numeric codes before using arbitrary imported data. Invalid code points can produce invalid Unicode; surrogate values are excluded here. A code point is not necessarily an entire displayed grapheme.
scenarios: Reconstruct known two-symbol labels from numeric code records.
Inspect a local table of Unicode values as readable text.
Build a report sample containing symbols that are awkward to type directly.
title: Turn code points into labels
problem: Return id and char(first_code, second_code) AS text for every row, ordered by id. Use the argument order as given. Inputs contain valid nonzero Unicode scalar values.
hint: Pass both integer columns to char in one call.
goal: Use char() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
